mission: Test whether the later-successful Agent-first responsibility-placement selection rule predicts historical candidate disposition better than naive persistence/current-convenience/architecture-symmetry baselines using evidence frozen before each disposition.
questionOrHypothesis: Were Agent-first reforms successful because a better selection mechanism identified durable responsibilities, or would simpler baselines have predicted the same outcomes?
evidenceSelection: Eight to twelve Computing historical candidate cases with exact pre-disposition Git evidence and later disposition oracle. Pre-evidence must precede the scored outcome; later documents may define oracle only, not features.
strongBaseline: B2 cross-cutting usefulness/architecture symmetry => shared layer
minimalCandidateOrNoChange: M-RESP predicts disposition from repeated observed burden, simpler-baseline failure, future-model robustness, owner clarity, authority-duplication risk, measurable consequence and second-consumer pressure.
independentOracle: Later canonical Computing responsibility map, historical compression evidence, Agent-first promotion decision and ACS closeout bound to exact Git revisions.
developmentSplit: First half of chronology may refine feature coding definitions only; model rules are frozen before scoring later cases.
holdoutSplit: At least three later cases including A0/ACS-era decisions must not alter model rules.
invalidityConditions: feature coding uses evidence published after the disposition
candidate outcome is ambiguous under the oracle
scoring rules change after holdout inspection
historical candidate identity cannot be bound to exact Git evidence
authorityBoundary: Computing research only; no owner source mutation and no claim that retrospective prediction proves causal necessity.
budget: Use existing Git/evidence plus deterministic analysis; no Provider required for F1 scoring.
stopRule: Stop after the frozen case set is scored and at least one counterexample to the leading model is inspected.
deletionOrNoChangeOutcome: If M-RESP does not materially beat simple baselines, do not use Agent-first success as evidence for a PAL responsibility mechanism.
rollbackRule: Research-only files may be deleted; owner state is untouched.
publicationBoundary: Computing-local evidence only until cross-case result is stable.
